title: No virtual DOM, and what that changes about how you think

videos.script:
Press a button in a React app, {{react}} and React calls your component again. It gets back a description of the whole component. It compares it with the last one. Then it changes the one piece of text that differs.

That description is the virtual DOM. {{vdom}} It is a good idea, and Svelte does not have one.

Today you see what Svelte does instead. {{once}} First, a component whose script runs once. You will press a button three times and watch the script stay quiet.

Then signals. {{signals}} A signal is a value that remembers who read it. When it changes, it tells exactly those readers, and nobody else.

Then you count. {{count}} The browser can report every change made to the page. You will press a button and see one change, on one piece of text.

And then the honest part. {{honest}} A virtual DOM ends at the same single change. The difference is all the work it did to find it.

Last, what this changes about how you write components. {{think}} Some habits from React you can drop. A few you have to keep.
